title: Askia Muhammad's pilgrimage from Gao to Mecca, c. 1496–1498
summary: In 1496 the new ruler of the Songhai empire went on the hajj, with 500 horsemen and 1,000 foot, gave freely on the way, set up a house for West African pilgrims at Medina, and came home to Gao nearly two years later, 50,000 ducats in debt but with the titles al-Hajj and khalifa that made Islam a pillar of his rule. Wikipedia dates it 1496 in one place and 1497–98 in another. The source gives no route: the line is the usual pilgrim road from the Sudan by Cairo, drawn straight.

legs.source: Askia Muhammad I (Wikipedia): the source names Mecca and Medina and no road; Cairo and the desert stages are the usual pilgrim road, not his
legs.doubt: The only source used names no route; the line is the usual way a ruler of the Sudan went to Mecca, and may not be his.

legs.source: Askia Muhammad I (Wikipedia): to Mecca and on to Medina; the Red Sea crossing and the Hejaz road are drawn straight

events.label: Mecca and Medina, the titles of al-Hajj and khalifa
events.text: He made many charitable gifts, set up a lodging for West African pilgrims in Medina, and returned to Gao having run up 50,000 ducats in debt. The titles he took home strengthened him at home.
events.doubt: Wikipedia dates the hajj 1496 in the body and 1497–98 in the opening paragraph.
